# `get_saved_photometry_stars`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

List the saved photometry plots in summary form.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | PURE GETTER / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable) |
| Side-effect tier | A |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xb6040, GetSavedPhotoMetryStars @0x202a70 (64-bit build) |

Iterates the cached plots, keeps those flagged saved and non-empty, and returns one summary each. Reads only the in-memory cache; no file is read. An empty selection is a success with an empty list.

Side effects: Builds and sorts a request-local vector under the photometry mutex. No file read, no persistent cache change, no camera requirement, no time limit shown.

Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_saved_photometry_stars"`. [READ] |
| `params` | any | no | - | Not read. Omission, null, object, scalar and array all take the same path. Clients SHOULD omit it. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

The handler has a generic failure branch but the helper returns success on ordinary paths. Whether the common logger writes are reachable on this path was not shown, hence the pure-getter grade (probable).

## Example

Request, request:

```json
{"id":121,"method":"get_saved_photometry_stars"}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_saved_photometry_stars","result":{"PhometryStars":[{"id":"plot-1","save":true,"startTime":"2026-01-31 21:15:00","radec_deg":[210.8,54.3],"star_name":"Example target"}]},"code":0,"id":121}
```
